Build School

A clear path from a parts list to a working PC. Keep the manuals and unresolved checks beside you.

Start a parts listPlan the complete cost

Explore interactive hardware diagrams

1. Plan the whole purchase

Write down the workloads, display, space and new spending limit. Inventory reused parts before choosing a platform. Keep absent prices visibly unknown.

Continue this step

2. Understand the parts

A processor, board, memory, storage, cooling, case and power supply work as a system. Discrete graphics are needed only for the workloads and outputs that require them.

Continue this step

3. Resolve compatibility

Use the readiness report, then read exact support documents for checks the catalog cannot certify. A passed socket check does not establish BIOS support or clearance.

Continue this step

4. Prepare and assemble

Use the case and component manuals for installation order, standoffs, cooler mounting and cable connections. Never open a PSU or assume modular cables are interchangeable.

Continue this step

5. Check cables and first boot

Before power-on, inspect the completed connections against the manuals. If there is no display, follow safe, observable checks before repeated disassembly.

Continue this step

6. Set up and record a baseline

Use official OS installation media and exact device drivers. Check recognition and basic operation before optional profiles; save the starting configuration.

Continue this step

Your build checklist

Progress is saved only in this browser. No account is required. Checking a box records your confirmation; it does not certify hardware safety or fit.

Keep the exact documents with your build

Use your build notebook to record model-specific manuals and checks. Before assembly, review cooler mounting and fit.

Installation positions and firmware procedures differ between models and revisions. Open your selected product’s source documentation in the builder. The links below demonstrate a documented example; they are not universal instructions.

  • MSI MAG B650 TOMAHAWK WIFI manual
  • CORSAIR PSU cable compatibility
  • Official Windows 11 installation media

If a step fails, use the troubleshooting path. A purchase is not the default fix.
